key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden, often with anxiety or stress trigger. LOCATION: Chest (variable location, can be diffuse or left-sided). DURATION: Minutes to hours, typically peaks at 10 minutes. CHARACTER: Sharp or vague discomfort, "can't catch breath", chest tightness. AGGRAVATING: Anxiety, stress, hyperventilation. RELIEVING: Reassurance, breathing exercises, anxiolytics. TIMING: Episodic, associated with stress/anxiety. SEVERITY: 5-8/10 subjectively but benign objectively. KEY POSITIVES: Hyperventilation, perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm, sense of impending doom, young patient, history of anxiety disorder, dyspnea out of proportion to findings. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT exertional pattern, NOT cardiac risk factors typically, NOT reproducible with palpation.

red_flags: Cardiac risk factors present (must rule out cardiac)
First episode ever in older patient
